processing: Thirteen cues for a Farmer at work in a field (doc 42, Fields). Six strokes of a mattock digging a garden as foley for the copper hoe biting the ground (a mattock, not a hoe; it is the heavier tool, so the high-pass at 100 Hz turns its thud down). The upload repeats one stretch of itself, and the six are cut from the first copy of that stretch or from the part after it that is not repeated. One plant pulled up out of the ground with its roots snapping, and three tears of a weed as foley for a crop pulled (a weed torn, not a crop), for a ripe tile being pulled; the plant's upload begins on its first snap, so that cue fades in over the recording's first 4 ms. Three strokes of a hand brushing the ground as foley for a tile sown by hand (no seed is heard); that recording is quiet, so its own hiss stands 16 to 18 dB under the strokes. Each variant is a separate recorded event. Cropped to start on the event, DC removed, gently high- and low-pass filtered (zero phase), edge-faded and set to the level below subject to its peak ceiling. No synthesis, pitch shifting, time stretching, added reverberation or denoising. Each cue has its own target so that its kind's variants measure alike by the A-weighted level of their loudest eighth of a second: the hoe at -26 dB, the pull at -29 dB, the sowing at -27 dB. Runtime cosmetic pitch variation remains.
